title: Share Quiver and Heptapod engagement rules and promote range/lock settings
context: Owner requested architecture/parity after repeated lab/game drift. DART presentation was shared, but gameplay ignored authored engagement bands and Quiver accumulated a lock against its tower cell rather than the acquired enemy. Lock knobs were not represented in reviewed defaults.
outcome: The pure missile-targeting owner now handles target retention, inclusive ground-distance bands, immediate lock reset after target loss/switch and firing eligibility. Lock/guidance and the Heptapod loop moved behind top-level compatibility facades into domain modules. Gameplay supplies sphere arcs and actual post-slew aim; lab supplies flat ground metres. A fixed 10 authoring metres per cell is independent of fitted asset scale. The shipped 30 m maximum therefore becomes three base cells, replacing old game Quiver 3.5/Heptapod 3.4 ranges; existing 8% upgrade range growth remains and minimum range stays fixed. Version 5 adds per-family lock gate/time/break and aim tolerance to reviewed presets, with strict v2/v3/v4 migration including saved metadata baselines and generated content. Heptapod retains hard-target policy, cassette, standoff, leash and return/reload, and cannot walk into a narrow blind zone. Game damage/economy/progression and cadence are preserved; lab fixtures remain general test targets and drive speed/recoil/cadence controls are explicitly preview-only. This is missile engagement/presentation parity, not full combat-engine extraction. User project drafts remain v4 on disk, readable as v5 with their Quiver 9–40 m and Heptapod 9–36 m values intact; neither was promoted. One local source server was restarted at port 8155 for the updated schema.
alternatives: Deriving engagement reach from fitted model size was rejected because mesh replacement or tier appearance would change combat range.
Keeping separate lab and game locks was rejected because progress could transfer between enemies and authored changes remained misleading.
A strict floating-point comparison initially excluded sphere endpoints a few ulps beyond the band; a one-nanometre conversion tolerance preserves inclusive boundaries without a gameplay-sized margin.
evidence: npm test: 73 test programs pass, including old lock/guidance and Heptapod lifecycle invariants.
npm run check: 24 pure-layer modules, canonical module identity, pinned kernel/assets and current preset validation pass.
npm run test:browser: complete source acceptance passes.
node scripts/browser-test.mjs --missile-parity: actual Quiver/Heptapod combat targeting, arrivals, blind-zone exclusion, pause and restart pool cleanup pass.
node scripts/browser-test.mjs --local-authoring: real GUI lock edit, isolated save/review/apply, gameplay consumption of promoted range/lock settings, checks/build and exact undo pass.
test/missile-targeting.mjs: flat/sphere selection equivalence, exact endpoints, target changes, cooldown, unavailable pool and paused lock progress.
test/heptapod.mjs: narrow engagement band, paused state and unavailable-launcher cassette preservation.
Local server state returns stalheart-fx-5; both existing project draft files and their original baselines parse without writes.
